chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
title: Muggsy, Darnell Howard, Pops Foster and old Chicago bassists
summary: Chat about where Muggsy, Darnell Howard and Pops Foster are now, and about bassists Eddie Garland and Bill Johnson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. That's... Muxley was called to keep getting that. I hear that he's still...
Yeah, he's been working with Earl Hines. I heard him last year in California.
Yeah, yeah. And Darnell Howard. Oh, yes. I know he had a group. He was here in Chicago. I didn't get to see him.
Pops Foster. Did you ever work with him, the bass player?
No, no, no. Never worked with Pops Foster. In fact, I didn't know...I don't think I met him.
He didn't come around Chicago much. Mostly St. Louis, New Orleans, St. Louis, and then New York.

Yeah, I heard a lot of him but I never, never...and he's out in California too. Yeah, working with Hines and Muxley and Darnell. Oh, no. Well, listen, what become of Eddie White was a bass...I never know. He was from Louisiana. He was with Joe Oliver when I first came around Chicago. He played bass with Joe. It was...I think it was Eddie Garland. Oh, Eddie Garland. Yeah.

Oh, yes. I saw him in California. Yeah. Had a nice interview with him. Yeah. Yeah. Looks good. Same as ever. Yeah. Eddie Garland. He's more bald than I am. Is that so? He gets around good. He's about 70 years old.
Yeah. Eddie's up in age now. Yeah. But he's active. Yeah. Well, that guy, I used to love to hear him play bass. Yeah, he really slaps that.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, he, I think... Bill Johnson. Bill Johnson. I'm trying to find him again. I haven't seen him in years. I don't know what become of Bill.
Mm-hmm. Bill was... But he said he went to Mexico, maybe. Yeah.
That's what I heard of, that he was down to Mexico or something. I haven't seen him for over ten years.
No, I haven't seen him for a long time. And, you know, he's...Bill is where?
Oh, he's about 86 or 87, I believe now.
Yeah, yeah. Bill Bull is right now.
